R203.note: Argv list without shell=True closes the injection vector; disclosed extra filename validation is harmless defense-in-depth.

R204.note: Correct JNDI parameterized search(name, filterExpr, filterArgs, cons) overload with RFC4515-escaped args; SearchControls() matches the default the null cons implied.

R205.note: SecureRandom.nextFloat() is a drop-in replacement preserving return type and downstream usage.

R206.note: sanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, rawBody) is the correct Angular API and preserves allowed tags while stripping script vectors.

R207.note: crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') is a proper CSPRNG source; longer code length has no functional downside for a Map key.

R208.note: Same correct parameterized JNDI search overload as R204, with explicit SearchControls preserving default search semantics.

R209.note: pool.execute() with ? placeholder correctly parameterizes the query; write-up overstates that pool.query() placeholders aren't safe, but the applied fix itself is sound and behavior-preserving.

R210.note: Jakarta Mail Session/MimeMessage/Transport fully removes manual SMTP command concatenation, but silently changes output: envelope.getSubjectLine() moves from the message body into the Subject header and the body is replaced with a hardcoded 'Ticket acknowledgement' string, losing the original body content without being called out.

R211.note: Removing @csrf_exempt restores standard CSRF middleware validation; matches the stated contract for authenticated+valid-token, missing-session, and non-POST cases.

R212.note: smtp.sendmail() is the correct high-level replacement for raw docmd() concatenation, but it silently drops the explicit EHLO identity ('bounce-notifier.example.com'), so the relay now sees the machine's default local hostname instead - an unstated protocol-visible change.

R213.note: long-cast multiply with Integer.MAX_VALUE bound check and Math.toIntExact() correctly detects overflow before allocation and returns 400 as specified; behavior openly described.

R214.note: firebase/php-jwt Key/JWT::decode is the correct verified-signature API, but the fix ships a literal placeholder key ('your-rsa-public-key-here') so as written it rejects every token until a real key is supplied - disclosed as a required follow-up, not silent.

R215.note:
Removing mark_safe() closes the XSS vector, but it also causes Django's template auto-escaping to escape the intentional wrapper markup (
...
) for every legitimate announcement, not just malicious ones; this loses the intended formatting and is not mentioned in the write-up.

R216.note: encode_entities() (verified empirically) escapes <, >, &, ", and ' by default, closing the sink without touching unrelated code.

R217.note: Scoping get_queryset() to owner for all users correctly closes the missing-authorization gap, but it also removes all list access for staff/agents (who previously could at least see tickets, however over-broadly) since no assigned_to field exists; the write-up discloses this as a known limitation pending a schema change.

R218.note: htmlspecialchars(..., ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') at the sink neutralizes the concatenated message string; no embedded markup was intended in that string so legitimate content is unaffected.

R219.note: Adds the missing $_FILES['avatar']['error'] check before use and checks move_uploaded_file()'s return value, correctly ordered ahead of the MIME probe; no change to the successful-upload path.

R220.note: Verified empirically with a live Microsoft.Extensions.Logging console run: LogWarning("...{Username}", username) produces byte-identical output to the original string-interpolated call when username contains CRLF - the forged multi-line log entry is unaffected; the structured-logging template does not neutralize embedded CR/LF for the default console/text formatter, so the reported vector is not closed.
